verdict.reason: No blocking finding in my scope. D59 is CLOSED on its Founder §13 criterion: my unchanged first-week grid gives E = O = B = 0 for NONE (90 cases, 264 exercises) and FAMILIAR (108, 408) and O = 0 for KNOWN (108, 408; E and B also 0); the return entry happens for every executed exercise; no block set is earned by the block in progress; the ceiling equals the last whole count executed before the break in every case measured (3,240 first-week exercises over moderate, long, 28/29-day and missed-target breaks, and 1,090 exercises of later-week returns); no count rises more than one set per executed whole week (B 0 everywhere; restoration grid A, B, C 0; 0 unexplained binding cap-weeks). D53 is CLOSED: no known equivalent state mode remains; the two boundaries found (a session on a break's stated first day; executions logged after the return) leave the return without a pre-break count by the Founder's own temporal invariants and the record as reported, so no declared ceiling is bypassed, and a newer report of the same break restores the entry and ceiling. D56, D57 and D58 hold. S-A to S-H are approved, S-C, S-D and S-H with recorded costs or boundaries. No policy text, clinical semantics or Founder decision is needed for the ruling. Five non-blocking findings are routed.

d53.basis: The original paths stay corrected (restoration grid and caps at 0), D56 and D57 hold, and D59, the known equivalent state mode that kept D53 open, is closed. I searched for further modes in my remit: later-week returns (ceiling equality 1,090 exercises), rotated-in exercises (24 cases: in the start state at the entry with their executed count as the ceiling; afterwards the declared D51/D52 path), re-establishments before a break (moderate: the re-establishment count is the ceiling; short: effort-guided re-establishment and one set per executed whole week), short breaks during the return steps, and separate breaks. None lets a known count come back faster than the declared rules. Two boundaries are not restoration modes: a session on a break's stated first day is read as after the break began (Founder I4, I6, P4; INTERRUPTION_CONTRACT §5), and executions logged after a return are read only by a newer report of the same break (record as reported). In both the return holds no pre-break count for those exercises, the dose is the policy's untrained establishment (2 sets or fewer at RIR 3 or more), and a newer report of the same break restores the entry and ceiling (72 same-day cases: 195 of 195 exercises; late-log probe: E, O, B 0). They are routed as NF-1 and R37. The engineering judge rules on identity and causality in parallel.

rulings.ruling: APPROVED. An exercise first executed in the break's week enters a moderate or long return at the entry (1 set, RIR 4 or more), with its last executed whole count as the ceiling: the declared strengthReturnSets applied to the state at the break, as my R7A1-SSCTR-r2 required change stated. Extended grid: E, O, B and ceiling disagreements 0 for NONE, FAMILIAR and KNOWN at 14, 21, 28, 29 and 42 days; rotation spot-check: rotated-in exercises likewise.

APPROVED. After a short break a loaded exercise whose first log the break left unadopted has no load reference and is established by effort again: UNLOGGED, at most effortGuidedLoad.sets (2), RIR 3 or more, at its executed repetitions (1,620 short-return exercises: first exposure never above max(last executed count, 2), never below RIR 3, never at other repetitions; no calendar week above the no-break twin's). A bodyweight exercise set up before a short break continues at its normal count (observed first counts equal to or below the pre-break count). This is SSCTR D52 applied, and "resume the last completed doses" is respected. Non-blocking: the row's note says "No usable load was logged last time" when a load was logged but not yet adopted (NF-4, explainability).

APPROVED as the declared reading. An exposure that missed its logged target is performed (in use, last performed date kept) but gives no ceiling count, the same "executed" reading the weekly transition has used since R6 (D49); the ceiling falls back as declared (an earlier executed count, else the known count, else the normal count). Missed-target family (153 cases): E, O against the declared fallback, B and ceiling disagreements 0. Rises stay one set per executed whole week, gated on post-return targets. Recorded asymmetry (R36): a missed target can leave a higher ceiling than a met one (re-establishment probe: 4 against 2); the next policy revision may decide whether a performed count bounds the ceiling.

APPROVED. A re-establishment executed before a break is a fact: a moderate or long return takes the re-establishment count as the ceiling (the literal "last set count executed before the break"; probe: back-squat 2, entry 1@4, step 1, then 2 sets held to the horizon); after a short break the load is established by effort again (UNLOGGED 2@3, under the earlier load) and the count comes back one set per executed whole week, the regain ending after a whole week (trace: never above the no-break timeline's week). Recorded cost (R35): an establishment-capped ceiling holds the count at 2 until a later completed development block, so one 2-set session inside a 7-week gap lowers the ceiling below the count the regain was restoring; a lower set count costs adaptation if it persists (R6-S52, full text). Conservative and declared; for the next policy revision.

APPROVED. Two separate short breaks each get their own easy slot (I9); when the first break's slot is still ahead, the second takes the next quality slot because an eased run is no longer a quality slot (my R7A1-r2 reading a), so both run easy; a newer report of the same break keeps its single slot. Probe: Tuesday of weeks 5 and 6 eased, each carrying its break's identity, the next quality held at THRESHOLD 41 until executed quality; same-break correction: one slot. The cost (one more eased quality session per additional reported break) keeps every dose at or below the planned and held doses (R6-S14: maintained intensity matters when volume falls, which supports one slot per break, not more).

APPROVED. A short break during the return steps resumes the step reached; a weekly review decided after the break began does not count (Founder I6, I7). Probe: break Thursday to Sunday of the re-entry week, return Monday: week 6 repeats RETURN_ENTRY, week 7 RETURN_STEP, runs stay RETURN (15/15/20); break after the re-entry week's review: step 2 (2 sets) resumes, runs 30/30/45; no row at the dose before the first break. Cost: one repeated entry week, conservative.

APPROVED. The entry repetition target of an exercise first executed before the break is the one it was executed at (an accessory's 7, not the goal's 5): 0 mismatches over every first-executed exercise of the extended grid. Observation outside the delta (NF-5, no action): a known-state exercise whose rows the goal range clamps (db-bench-press known 3x8, rows of 6) enters at its known 8 repetitions, 1 set at RIR 4 or more with an effort-chosen load capped at the known load; unchanged since R6 and not material.

APPROVED as a declared boundary. A return reads the executions recorded by its report; an execution before the break logged after the return is read by a newer report of the same break, never retroactively (append-only record, no replay). Probe: unknown at the return, the exercises get the untrained establishment (FIRST_ESTABLISH 2@3, then the normal count: NONE E 5, B 5; FAMILIAR E 7, B 6), which is not a restoration of a known count; reported again, SAME_BREAK with the entry and ceiling 2 (E, O, B 0). Routed (R37): prompt a newer report of the same break when a session dated before a reported break is logged after its return.

newRecords.basis: The sporting behaviours S-A to S-H of the state at a break and the break identity; prescriptive, so it has a queue item.

newFindings.title: A session on a break's stated first day is not part of the state at the break
newFindings.finding: A break covers its whole first day (INTERRUPTION_CONTRACT §5, applying Founder I4, I6, P4), so a session executed and logged that day is read as after the break began. For an exercise executed only that day, the return holds no pre-break count: in the first loaded week it gets the untrained establishment (72 cases: NONE E 51 of 51, O 140, B 16; FAMILIAR E 60 of 72, O 188; KNOWN O 16). A newer report of the same break starting the next day is SAME_BREAK and restores the entry with the executed count as the ceiling for 195 of 195 exercises (E, O, B 0).
newFindings.whyNotBlocking: It is the Founder's temporal invariant applied to the athlete's stated dates, not a state mode that ignores a known pre-break count; the dose given is the policy's untrained establishment (2 sets or fewer, RIR 3 or more, effort-chosen); and a correction path exists. A sporting reading would rather start the break after the last executed session.
newFindings.owner: Product/UX with Data (G03, joint), then the runtime author
newFindings.recommendation: When a break's stated first day holds an executed session, ask whether the break began after it (ASK), or derive the start from the last executed session; never resolve it silently.

newFindings.title: An establishment-capped count as the return ceiling
newFindings.finding: The literal ceiling ("the last set count executed before the break") makes a first establishment or a re-establishment count (2 sets) the ceiling until a later completed development block; one 2-set re-establishment inside a 7-week gap lowers the ceiling below the count the regain was restoring (probe: 2 sets held to the horizon against 4 without the break). A lower set count costs adaptation if it persists (R6-S52, full text; R7A2-S01, abstract).
newFindings.owner: Runtime author with Product Constitution & Governance, SSCTR review
newFindings.recommendation: The next policy revision may decide whether an establishment-capped count bounds the ceiling, or the regain target does (still one set per whole week).

newFindings.title: Met and missed targets give different ceilings
newFindings.finding: A missed-target exposure gives no ceiling count, so the ceiling falls back to an earlier executed count, the known count or the normal count, which can be higher than the met-target ceiling (re-establishment probe: 4 against 2). Rises are still one set per executed whole week, gated on post-return targets.
newFindings.owner: Next policy revision (Product Constitution & Governance), SSCTR review
newFindings.recommendation: Decide whether a performed count, met or not, bounds the ceiling (for example the lower of the performed count and the fallback).

newFindings.title: UNLOGGED note after a short break
newFindings.finding: The re-establishment row after a short break says "No usable load was logged last time" when the athlete did log a load before the break that was not yet adopted.
newFindings.recommendation: Say that the load logged before the break is not yet confirmed and will be chosen by effort again.

newFindings.title: Return entry repetitions of a known exercise
newFindings.finding: A known-state exercise whose rows the goal range clamps enters the return at its known repetitions (db-bench-press known 3x8, rows of 6: entry 8 repetitions, 1 set, RIR 4 or more, load capped at the known load); unchanged since R6.
newFindings.recommendation: No action; re-read at the next policy revision.
